page: Microsoft Azure E1pds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this configuration provides a single dedicated vCPU paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation ratio. The host hardware provisions 59 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage integration. It contains no graphics accelerators and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

With its ARM architecture and dense memory-to-core footprint, the E1pds_v7 delivers efficient resource balance for applications demanding memory capacity without requiring multi-core compute concurrency. The integrated local NVMe drive delivers high-throughput ephemeral read and write performance directly on the hypervisor host. However, the presence of a single core and lack of x86-specific instruction sets introduce tradeoffs for compute-intensive pipelines and software stacks that have not been compiled for arm64 execution.

The hardware configuration makes the Microsoft Azure E1pds_v7 suitable for low-footprint in-memory caches, small key-value datastores, lightweight relational database instances, staging environments, and ARM-targeted background microservices.
description: Microsoft Azure E1pds_v7 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 1 dedicated vCPU built on the 64-bit ARM architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 59 GB of local NVMe SSD storage with support for Premium Storage configurations. It does not provision discrete GPUs and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Designed for memory-centric operational requirements on ARM hardware, the instance provides cost-effective efficiency for applications that prioritize memory space over multi-core parallel throughput. The presence of fast local NVMe storage facilitates rapid temporary caching and I/O tasks. While single-vCPU ARM execution limits suitability for compute-heavy parallel workloads, the E1pds_v7 is well structured for lightweight in-memory data stores, small database nodes, caching layers, and ARM-native development or microservices tasks.
